title: “A brain refused the key” in {name}: what it means, how to fix it
description: When {name} says a brain refused the key, the service behind it said no. Make a new key on its site, and put it in Settings › Brains.
answer: The service behind the brain said no to the key {name} gave it. Make a new key on that service’s site, then open {settings} › {brains}, the brain that says {trouble}, and press {change}.
tour.trouble: Here are your brains. The one whose key was refused says {trouble}: open it.
parts: The key was copied with a letter missing or a space too many; it was deleted or ran out on the service’s site; or the account behind it was closed. A key that Google Cloud Shell printed works for an hour only.
steps: Open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {brains}. The brain whose key was refused says {trouble}: open it.
On its service’s site, make a new key, and copy it.
Under {key}, press {change}, paste the new key, and press {connect}.
Or connect another brain instead, with {add}.
good: Under an answer, the same message has a button that opens the brain’s page.
Each time you open {brains}, {name} asks every brain again: once the new key works, {trouble} goes away.
A key stays on this device, encrypted, and goes only to its own service.
fixes: The new key is refused too
Look at the account on the service’s site: some ask for a payment method before a key works. Or start for free with OpenRouter: {choose}.
You don’t know which service it is
The brain is named after it, in {brains} and in the message: “… refused the key” starts with its name.
